Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the run chase. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Samara Ramnath and Asabi Callender walk in with their blades for West Indies Women Under-19. Rashmika Sewwandi has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, chasing this formidable total will be a tough task for the West Indies against a disciplined Sri Lankan attack. A steady and solid Powerplay will be crucial to set the tone for the rest of the chase. As for Sri Lanka, they'll aim to replicate their disciplined performance against Malaysia and stay on the money right from the first ball. Back in a bit for the chase.

Sanjana Kavindi is in for a chat. She says that she is happy and proud to play for her country. Adds that India's Shubman Gill is her favourite player and she likes the way he gives starts to his team.

From there, the batting side quickly took control through Sanjana Kavindi and captain Manudi Nanayakkara. While West Indies managed to create brief moments of pressure by picking up a couple of quick wickets during the middle phase, they were unable to maintain it consistently. Towards the end, they struck twice in quick succession to pull things back slightly as Sri Lanka seemed poised to surpass 180 but 166 is still a formidable total.

Sri Lanka finish with a commanding 166, setting a new tournament record for the highest total, surpassing their previous best of 162 scored against Malaysia just a couple of days ago. West Indies were their own worst enemies, conceding a staggering 36 extras, the most in any innings in the history of this competition, and faltering with both their catching and ground fielding. The start was promising for West Indies as they maintained disciplined lines and lengths, putting Sri Lanka under some pressure in the first three overs.
Short, on off, Shashini Gimhani slaps it over mid off for a brace. Sri Lanka Women Under-19 end their innings at 166/5!

A defeat here will not be the end of the road, but if that happens and Malaysia lose to India, the game between West Indies and Malaysia will effectively be a knockout, with the winner advancing. Sri Lanka started their tournament on a high, dominating Malaysia with a comprehensive 139-run victory. With two games remaining, it is unlikely that Sri Lanka will miss out on a Super Six spot unless things go drastically wrong. Hello one and all, and welcome to yet another exciting Group A double-header day in Kuala Lumpur! In the first game of the day, West Indies will face Sri Lanka at the Bayuemas Oval. Later on, the defending champions India will take on the tournament hosts, Malaysia.
... MATCH DAY ...

Match 15 of the 2025 ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup sees West Indies Women Under-19 take on Sri Lanka Women Under-19 at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur. This Group A clash brings together two teams with contrasting starts to the tournament. Sri Lanka dominantly opened their campaign, brushing aside tournament debutants Malaysia, while West Indies were handed a heavy defeat by defending champions India. West Indies’ batting struggles were evident in their opener, with Asabi Callender and Kenika Cassar the only batters offering resistance. To bounce back, they will need strong performances from captain Samara Ramnath, Jahzara Claxton, and Naijanni Cumberbatch. On the bowling front, Jahzara Claxton and Selena Ross will be crucial with the new ball, and disciplined lines and lengths will be key to containing Sri Lanka’s batters. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, delivered a polished performance against Malaysia. Sanjana Kavindi, Dahami Sanethma, and Hiruni Kumari all made valuable contributions, with Dahami scoring a fine fifty. Captain Manudi Nanayakkara and Sumudu Nisansala will be eager to leave their mark in this game. The bowling unit was equally impressive, with slow left-arm orthodox bowler Chamudi Praboda standing out. Sri Lanka’s sharp catching and ground fielding added to their all-around professionalism, making them a tough side to beat. Will Sri Lanka make it two from two, or will West Indies bounce back to secure their first points? We shall find out.
